Subject: Regulatory readiness & evaluation roadmap for Bennett Health (NIST / EU AI Act)

Hi Sonia —

Thanks again for sharing the RFP. Attached is a concise, customer-facing evaluation and regression roadmap that aligns our operational controls to NIST AI RMF and provides a pragmatic mapping to EU AI Act obligations. The attached files are: Redwood-EvalPlan-v1.pdf (high-level cadence), EU-AI-Act-Mapping-Annex.xlsx (control mapping and suggested artifact list), and NIST-RMF-Matrix.docx (detailed traceability).

High-level notes:
- We treat classifiers/triage models as high-risk when they meet the Act’s Article 6 criteria; for those, we provide pre-deployment impact assessments, post-deployment monitoring metrics, and a 30/90/180-day regression cadence.
- For other application types we recommend a lighter sampling and automated drift checks with configurable thresholds.
- Evidence: we can provide SOC 2 reports, pen test summaries, KMS integration docs, and an exportable eval report tied to each model version.

Can we schedule a 45-minute walkthrough this week to go through the mapping and the audit artifacts you’ll need for procurement? Proposed: Wed 30 Jun at 15:00 CEST — Zoom link here: https://zoom.us/j/123456789.

If helpful I can also loop in Marcus to speak to the runtime/latency and Lauren for the compliance evidence packaging.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference

Camila / Lauren —

Quick update on the technical annex draft: attached is a short Word snippet (NIST-RMF-Annex-snippet.docx) that outlines our evaluation pipeline. Highlights:
- Pre-deployment: labeled seed test-suite (unit + slice tests), synthetic adversarial examples (documented), and a held-out clinical dataset for final acceptance.
- Post-deployment: continuous telemetry with stratified sampling (1% baseline -> auto-scale to 5% on drift), automated regression triggers (AUC drop > 3 absolute points OR task-specific failure mode), and an artifact store that pins model binaries + tokenizer + eval snapshot.
- We include a model version manifest with cryptographic hash and a link to the audit bundle.

I also added a short paragraph on quantization/approximation impacts and how we run comparative regression tests between FP16 and int8 variants to surface performance vs. quality trade-offs.

I can have the full annex and the sample latency/cost profiles by EOD.

- Marcus
